svg.text: Grey lattice = the uniform grid the 2-D FFT REQUIRES, the same in all three panels. Interpolation exists to move
each sample onto an intersection. Panel 3 is there; panels 1 and 2 are not, in different ways.
1 POLAR (Doerry Fig 3)
2 TRAPEZOIDAL (Doerry Fig 5)
3 RECTANGULAR -- on the grid
kr[i,j] = (2 pr[i]/c) (f0[i] + j df[i])
Pulse i is an arc at aspect angle phi_i. pr[i] is
the projection on the MEAN look direction, so kr
IS the k_y component. Neither axis lands on
the lattice yet.
PASS 1 (range): t = (KR[q] - x0_i) / dx_i
x0_i = 2 pr[i] f0[i]/c, dx_i = 2 pr[i] df[i]/c
Every pulse resampled onto the COMMON grid KR.
Since kr is the k_y component this makes k_y
uniform -- ROWS line up. k_x still carries an
angular increment: a trapezoid.
PASS 2 (azimuth): u = KC[q] / kr
bracket k by a merge scan on tan(phi)
k_x uniform too: every sample on an
intersection. A separable 2-D FFT applies, so
the hardware runs two 1-D passes with a
transpose -- the corner-turn -- between.
